speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what are the causes of the reported food poisoning symptoms in students at the School of the Arts who consumed ready-to-eat meals distributed as part of Total Defence activities; and (b) what microbiological and shelf-life studies are required by the Singapore Food Agency and conducted as part of Food Resilience Preparedness Programme product testing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment in view of the suspension of the Total Defence food resilience programme after the School of the Arts food poisoning incident (a) what processes are currently in place to vet suppliers of ready-to-eat meals for all Government programmes; and (b) whether there are plans to introduce more stringent checks or audits to ensure compliance with food safety regulations.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment with regard to the gastroenteritis outbreak among students at the School of the Arts after consuming ready-to-eat meals prepared by SATS at a Food Resilience Preparedness Programme on 18 February 2025 (a) how many meals were contaminated and whether the contamination extended to meals for other organisations such as active ageing centres; (b) what are the causes for the contamination; and (c) whether any penalties will be imposed against SATS.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These five Parliamentary Questions (PQs) relate to the food safety incident at the School of the Arts (SOTA).

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The RTE distribution was originally scheduled to take place from 15 February to 28 February.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Students who needed medical attention sought outpatient medical treatment and have since recovered.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the same time, we also reached out to other recipient institutions to ascertain if there were other cases of related illness.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Joint investigations by the Ministry of Health (MOH) and SFA are ongoing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: All affected individuals have received the necessary medical attention and have since recovered.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SFA has also collected samples of the meals for testing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SFA and MOH are conducting a comprehensive investigation of this incident, and SFA will take the necessary corrective and enforcement actions if lapses are detected.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members asked about the food safety processes applied to the supply of RTE meals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SATS, as an SFA-licensed establishment, is required to comply with food safety requirements and subjected to food safety inspections.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Food safety requirements include ensuring that food preparation areas and process workflows are set up in a way that prevent cross-contamination between raw and cooked food, putting systems in place to ensure cleanliness and freedom from pest infestation, as well as having food workers certified with food safety training.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SFA inspected SATS’ premises on 23 January 2025, prior to the start of the FRPP.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The premises were found to be clean and no food safety violations were detected.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SATS had also put in place additional measures for FRPP.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Each meal produced under the FRPP was individually tested for leaks.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Further, an SFA-accredited laboratory conducted sample microbiological testing to ensure food safety.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members asked about steps taken to restore public confidence in the safety of RTE meals used in resilience programmes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We agree that we need to restore public confidence in the RTE meals.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As investigation is ongoing, it is too early to state the steps to take.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SFA will conduct an after-action review to draw and learn from the lessons of this episode.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: SFA will continue to engage stakeholders, including schools, food businesses and community partners on our FRPP.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have Clementi residents who followed this news and were understandably concerned that there were reports of food poisoning in conjunction with certain RTE meals.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have got two sets of supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: There were media reports that described the meals also as having real-time shelf-life studies.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Can I ask as part of these shelf-life studies, under what kind of storage temperatures the testing was done to test the shelf-life?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: And did these storage temperatures reflect the variation that can happen when such meals are stored in the community for longer periods of time?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Because weather can be warmer when these meals are being stored in a venue that may have sunlight coming from time to time, and so on?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: With regard to the first question about the conditions for testing, we believe that SATS had tested the RTE meals in the real-time, real case situations, simulating the transportation and storage conditions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: But Dr Tan is absolutely right in the sense that these are the questions that SFA and MOH, together with SATS, will ask as we review the entire exercise.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is important for us to learn from this exercise, including some of the test conditions, to make sure that this programme will evolve more robust than before.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As to the question of whether there was clustering, I think we are still getting the data.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We would like to provide a fuller picture after we have gone through the data.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First is while the Ministry conducts regular inspections to ensure compliance with food safety regulations, can the Ministry clarify whether these audits encompass the entire supply chain of RTE food production, from ingredient sourcing to final delivery?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And if certain stages are excluded, what are the reasons for these like omissions and how might they impact the overall safety of the food provided to Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And secondly, to enhance public trust, is the Ministry considering making food safety violations by suppliers more transparent?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: For instance, will there be a public registry of food safety lapses or penalties imposed on suppliers?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Of course, if you look at the entire value chain, not all of them are of the same risk.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, we need to take a risk-based approach, scientifically-based approach to dedicate and focus our inspection resources, so that we are more effective in ensuring food safety as a framework.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We do not want to draw any conclusion at this point in time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We want to do a fuller review and we will look at all possible causes of these gastroenteritis cases.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If they have many food infringements, they will be downgraded, they will be given more inspections audits along the way.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, our SFA officers will take a risk-based approach.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If there has been infringements in the past, we will inspect more frequently.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And by grading the caterers and food establishments, we are hoping to give that information, that transparency to buyers and consumers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can I ask the Minister how long will the review or the investigation take?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I think that we are working as quickly as we can.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The RTE meals are actually isolated and controlled, so we do not see that going into the public.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, there is no urgency from a food safety point of view.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The packages are all collected, so we are not continuing with this programme for the time being.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will do our best to do a study quickly, but more importantly is to get ourselves ready for the next programme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have to learn and take positive lessons from this programme.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: How do we get Singapore to be ready to be resilient to disruptions?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And the disruption is not just in food supply.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: What if we lack the facilities to cook food?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: How can we continue to provide nutritious food to the population in large numbers and in a way that is palatable to the population?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is in no means a small undertaking.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will have to learn from this lesson.
